newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Foreign investment in Brazil covers 40 pct c/a gap.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Brazil covers 40 pct c/a gap.

text.p: Direct foreign investment in Brazil reached $6.6 billion in the year to October 15, enough to finance 40 percent of the country's current account deficit, Finance Minister Pedro Malan was quoted as saying.

Malan, speaking to a meeting of cement produers in Rio, criticized "the short-term hysteria over the trade balance," but admitted the government was concerned about the current account, news wire Invest News reported.
The minister mentioned an International Monetary Fund study which referred to countries with current account deficits equivalent to eight percent of gross domestic product.
"Here, analysts decided that if the deficit goes above three percent of GDP, the real (currency) will have a heart attack and die on the spot," Malan was quoted as saying.
Brazil's current account deficit during the first nine months of the year was equivalent to 2.53 percent of GDP.

The government was taking steps to boost exports, including the exemption of the so-called ICMS tax which would benefit 40 percent of exporters, the revival of an export guarantee scheme and special credit lines.
Twenty-five percent of imports entering Brazil were capital goods, while a further 45 percent were classed as intermediate goods, Invest News quoted Malan as saying.
"That's a reasonable breakdown for a country like Brazil. We do not see any problem from growing exports," he said.
